decisive_items: occasional large, non-septate hyphae with irregular diameter and branching
multiple rounded, echogenic neoformations at the pyloric antrum
it had been fed a raw rabbit–based raw food (BARF) diet for 3 months
response.rationale: Cytology shows non-septate hyphae with irregular branching, characteristic of zygomycosis (phycomycosis), supported by gastric nodules and raw diet exposure. Basidiobolomycosis is a specific zygomycete but requires culture/PCR confirmation; phycomycosis is the broader, more appropriate syndromic diagnosis.

rejected.why: No foreign body identified; radiographs unremarkable and ultrasound shows nodules, not a foreign body.
Same as R1; clinical signs are nonspecific and contradicted by imaging findings.
Foodborne infection is too broad; cytology specifically indicates fungal hyphae, not bacterial/parasitic.
Neoplasia is possible but cytology demonstrates fungal organisms, making infection more likely.
Basidiobolomycosis is a specific zygomycete but not confirmed by culture/PCR; phycomycosis is the appropriate general category.
